name: extract-regex
description:
What a regular expression matches in a phrase, case-sensitive, searched anywhere.

pattern: the regular expression; \w, \b and \d take Cyrillic letters too.
all_matches: extract gives every match, joined by a space; by default the first.
invert: the found part is the text the pattern does not match: remove keeps only the matches, joined with nothing between («диван 120x200» with \d+ → «120200»); extract gives the text outside the matches («диван x»); find marks the phrases where such text is left.

find marks the phrases where the pattern matches; remove cuts out every match; extract gives the first match.

Example: semkit read --text "диван 120x200" extract-regex "\d+x\d+" write -
-> 120x200

extract-regex keeps only what the matcher finds in the working column; an empty cell where it finds nothing.

options.name: --pattern
options.description: the regular expression; \w, \b and \d take Cyrillic letters too.

options.name: --all-matches
options.description: extract gives every match, joined by a space; by default the first.

options.name: --invert
options.description: the found part is the text the pattern does not match: remove keeps only the matches, joined with nothing between («диван 120x200» with \d+ → «120200»); extract gives the text outside the matches («диван x»); find marks the phrases where such text is left.

options.name: --as
options.description: Write the result to a new column NAME and keep the working column as it is.

arguments.name: PATTERN
arguments.description: the regular expression; \w, \b and \d take Cyrillic letters too. The same as --pattern PATTERN.
